title: Timeline Glitch
blurb: History's calendar is glitching. Three of these really line up. One is pure cap.

cards.say: Cleopatra [lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid], [was born about 250 years after Alexander the Great died], [ruled Egypt as queen for more than 40 years before Rome took over], and [was staying in Rome when Julius Caesar was assassinated].
cards.real: Cleopatra ruled for about 21 years, from 51 BC until her death in 30 BC, when she was 39.

cards.say: Oxford University [got its first royal charter from King Henry VIII], [was teaching students before the Aztecs founded their capital city], [didn't let women earn degrees until after World War I], and [had a group of its scholars leave and help start Cambridge University].
cards.real: Oxford's first royal charter came in 1248, from King Henry III, long before Henry VIII's time.
src: https://www.bestcolleges.com/blog/how-old-is-the-university-of-oxford/ (Henry III issued the royal charter in 1248)

cards.say: The Hubble Space Telescope [went up into space before the first website went online], [was already in orbit when Google was founded], [launched with a main mirror that was ground to the wrong shape], and [took the first picture of a black hole while orbiting Earth].
cards.real: The first black hole photo, shown in 2019, came from the Event Horizon Telescope, a team of radio telescopes linked up around Earth.
src: https://sci.esa.int/web/hubble/-/37633-launch (launched April 24, 1990); https://www.engadget.com/2015/12/20/first-website-is-25-years-old/ (first website went live at CERN on December 20, 1990)

cards.say: The Great Pyramid of Giza [was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for more than 3,700 years], [took its builders about 90 years of work to finish], [was already more than 2,000 years old when Alexander the Great was born], and [has graffiti inside left by the work crews who built it].
cards.real: Most estimates say it took about 20 to 27 years to build, for the pharaoh Khufu, around 2600 BC.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza (tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza (built c. 2600 BC; Khufu's reign estimated 2700 to 2500 BC); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great (born 356 BC)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza (work-gang names painted in the relieving chambers)

cards.say: Tutankhamun [ruled Egypt more than 1,000 years after the Great Pyramid was built], [had the first royal tomb found in the Valley of the Kings], [became pharaoh when he was only eight or nine years old], and [had his tomb found the same year the BBC started broadcasting].
cards.real: Royal tombs there were found long before his, like Seti I's in 1817. Tut's, found in 1922, was famous because it was nearly intact.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutankhamun (tomb found November 1922); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC (formed October 18, 1922, first broadcast a few weeks later)

cards.say: The Colosseum [opened more than 100 years after Julius Caesar died], [had a giant sun awning worked by hundreds of sailors], [was already more than 1,100 years old when the Magna Carta was sealed], and [was opened by Emperor Nero with 100 days of games].
cards.real: Emperor Titus opened it in AD 80 with 100 days of games. Nero had died in AD 68, before work on it even began.
src: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Colosseum (hundreds of Roman sailors worked the velarium rigging)
https://www.britannica.com/topic/Colosseum (dedicated in 80 CE); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magna_Carta (sealed by King John on June 15, 1215)
https://www.britannica.com/topic/Colosseum (begun 70 to 72 CE under Vespasian, dedicated by Titus in 80 CE with 100 days of games)

cards.say: Leif Erikson [grew up in Norway, the homeland of his Viking ancestors], [reached North America about 500 years before Columbus], [landed in America before William the Conqueror invaded England], and [was the son of the explorer who gave Greenland its name].
cards.real: Leif was probably born in Iceland and grew up in Greenland, where his father, Erik the Red, founded the Viking settlement. He sailed to Norway as a young man.
src: https://www.worldhistory.org/Leif_Erikson (probably born in Iceland; Erik settled Greenland c. 985, where young Leif grew up)
https://www.worldhistory.org/Leif_Erikson (Erik the Red coined the name Greenland)

cards.say: Leonardo da Vinci [started painting the Mona Lisa after Columbus reached the Americas], [designed a robot knight more than 500 years ago], [was born while Joan of Arc was still alive in France], and [had his Mona Lisa stolen in 1911 and missing for over two years].
cards.real: Joan of Arc died in 1431. Leonardo was born in 1452, more than 20 years later.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo%27s_robot (designed in the late 15th century, prototype around 1495)

cards.say: Benjamin Franklin [was alive at the same time as Isaac Newton], [watched one of the first balloon flights to carry people, in Paris], [lived long enough to see George Washington become president], and [got rich from the patents on his inventions].
cards.real: Franklin never patented any of his inventions. He wrote that since we gain from the inventions of others, we should share ours freely.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Franklin (honored guest at the crewed balloon flight from the Tuileries, December 1, 1783)

cards.say: Orville Wright [was born while Abraham Lincoln was still president], [made his famous first flight while Harriet Tubman was still alive], [was still alive when a plane first flew faster than sound], and [kept that famous first flight in the air for just 12 seconds].
cards.real: Orville was born on August 19, 1871, six years after Lincoln died in April 1865.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wright_Flyer (first flight lasted 12 seconds, 120 feet, Orville at the controls)

cards.say: Sputnik 1 [went into orbit before NASA had even been created], [was a metal ball only about 23 inches wide], [launched closer in time to the first airplane flight than to the first iPhone], and [went up less than 12 years before people walked on the Moon].
cards.real: Sputnik went up in October 1957, almost 54 years after the first airplane flight in 1903 but less than 50 years before the first iPhone in 2007.

cards.say: Apollo 11 [touched down on the Moon before the first message was sent over the internet], [beamed its moonwalk to TV sets around the world in full color], [ended with its crew filling out a customs form back on Earth], and [landed less than 66 years after the Wright brothers' first flight].
cards.real: Apollo 11's live TV from the Moon's surface was black and white. Only its broadcasts from the spacecraft were in color.
src: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/air-space-magazine/live-from-the-moon-1882006/ (first lunar-surface TV was black and white, command module TV in color); https://www.parkes.atnf.csiro.au/news_events/apollo11/tv_from_moon.html (black-and-white slow-scan camera)
